question: Which of the following measures of credit control requires a well-developed money market?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Open market operations**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Open market operations** is a **credit control measure** that requires a well-developed money market
 
• Open market operations (OMOs) are a **quantitative instrument used by the central bank to buy and sell securities in the money and capital market**.
 
• This **affects the money supply in the economy, **which in turn controls credit creation.
 
• **For example, **the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) can sell securities to remove extra cash from the economy, which limits the money supply. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bank rate policy**

 
 
• The **central bank increases the bank rate** during inflation to raise the cost of bank credit.
 
• This d**iscourages businesses from borrowing, which decreases the volume of credit** and the level of economic activity
 
 
 
• **Variable reserve ratio**
 
 
• It refers to the **central bank's power to adjust the percentage of deposits that commercial banks are required to keep as reserves.**
 
• These reserves are either held in cash or as deposits with the central bank.
 
• This is an important aspect of monetary policy.
 
 
 
• **Qualitative measures**
 
 
• **These selective measures include margin requirements, consumer credit regulation, rationing of credit, and moral suasion. **
 
• These measures **do not directly affect the overall money supply** but control the conditions under which credit is given.
